brief.headline: Their cash is stuck for 101 days vs 64 for peers — offer to pay faster for a price cut worth their 12.16% borrowing rate

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price cut in exchange for paying them faster
priceAsk.target: A discount roughly matching their 12.16% borrowing cost on the amount we pay early
priceAsk.basis: Their cash is stuck for 101 days, much longer than similar firms at 64 days, so getting paid faster is worth real money to them. Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band (₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg), so there's room to move down while staying fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 days, in return for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹26.60 L of our cash, but the discount they give us should more than cover that cost

brief.financialLeverage: Shrinath is a ₹1064.86 Cr company, so our ₹6.47 Cr spend is just 0.61% of their revenue — we're a small customer, not a make-or-break one. They keep only 2.3% profit on every ₹100 they sell, so there's very little fat in their pricing. But their cash is stuck for 101 days (vs 64 for peers), and they borrow money at about 12.16%, so paying them faster is genuinely valuable to them. They also owe 1.25 times their own cash (₹282.62 Cr debt) and have had EPF payment delays, so cash is tight. Push for a trade — faster payment for a price cut — not a hard squeeze on price alone.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than similar firms
They borrow at a high rate, so early payment saves them real money
They already take longer to pay their own suppliers than most
Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band
evidence.figure: ₹205–305/kg typical ₹250/kg; verdict: MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)

evidence.point: We are a very small piece of their business
They keep very little profit, so room for price cuts is tight

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volume — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both film substrate and converts it — can second-source laminates at scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter for pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source option (health score D 31/100, revenue ₹222.04 Cr)

risks: They sit in the grey distress zone (Altman Z-score 2.36) and have EPF payment delays — push too hard and you risk tipping a fragile supplier; lead with supply security and qualifying a second source, not a price war
Their credit rating is only CARE BBB+ / Stable — middling; watch how much total volume you commit to them
They carry heavy debt (1.25x their equity, ₹282.62 Cr total) and cover interest payments only 1.94 times — a small but real supply-continuity risk if their cash gets tighter
We're just 0.61% of their revenue, so we have limited muscle to demand big concessions; the ask must be a fair trade, not a squeeze
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: Your cash is tied up much longer than your peers — 101 days vs 64 — so we'd like to offer you faster payment in exchange for a price adjustment that reflects the borrowing cost you'll save.
